title.narrative: Supporting local responses in White Nile, Gazira and Sennar to provide life-saving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable people

description.narrative: ltpgtThe situation in Sudan remains dire, with 26 million people in need of humanitarian assistance and 11.8 million displaced (OCHA). The project’s target states - White Nile, Gazira, and Sennar - are key to Sudan’s agricultural production. However, their proximity to the fluid frontlines and frequent conflict, including sporadic attacks by RSF and SAF, has led to increased displacement and heightened pressure on already scarce resources. This has further strained an already struggling agricultural system, disrupting food production.ltbrgtThe international humanitarian response has been severely restricted in accessing conflict-prone areas, limiting its ability to provide life-saving support. Amid these catastrophic needs and the largely absent or overstretched professional aid system, local mutual aid efforts have emerged as the most critical source of assistance for those affected by the conflict -19 months since its onset.ltbrgtThis mutual aid relies on voluntary, spontaneous, locally led responses, driven by crowdsourced information and sporadic international funding or crowdfunding. These mutual aid groups maximize available resources, using real-time, on-the-ground analysis to translate their unique knowledge into effective assistance for those affected.ltbrgtThe project will build on this mutual aid system with the objective of supporting community-led programming and mutual aid efforts to deliver timely, life-saving humanitarian assistance to conflict-affected populations in frontline areas, including White Nile, Gazira, and Sennar. To achieve this, DCA and SUDO will support 145 groups through a combination of capacity-strengthening activities and rapid, flexible financial support. This will enable MAGs to sustain their work in assisting themselves, their neighbors, and surrounding communities. ltbrgtThe project aims to reach 159,500 IDPs and vulnerable host communities with life-saving assistance. It will prioritize the most vulnerable groups, including women, adolescent girls and boys, the elderly, and youth impacted by the war, across all 24 localities in White Nile, Gazira, and Sennar.ltbrgtThe project will work closely with one L/NA SUDO, and capitalize on the effort made under CBPF-SUD-24-R-INGO-27622 to further enhance their relationship with MAGs in the three states. Building on best practices SUDO will utilize a phased transfer approach of mapping, identifying, verifying and training MAGs through community engagement in relevant themes for the context, including PSEA, AAP, protection mainstreaming, budgeting and reporting before transferring a grant of maximum 5,000USD for MAGs to implement their proposed initiatives. Priority will be given to women-led groups and groups focusing on activities for women. SUDO will continue to apply the Fsystem to engage with base MAG+ and their own contextualized project document system for other MAGs. SUDO will transfer 70 GCTs to MAGs, and DCA will directly transfer 55 grants. As a contingency plan to mitigate delays in banking delays and potential financial reconciliation gaps between partner transfers, this project has allocated 100,000USD for an Emergency Fund for MAGs. This fund will be administered by DCA and allows for direct cash transfers to MAGs by DCA through an informal financial service provider. DCA has an existing service agreement with FSPs in Uganda and can quickly transfer and distribute funding to groups via Bankak in a short time span. ltbrgtThe project will therefore have two delivery chains of supporting community-led programming 1) via a local partner layered with multiple training and lessons learned for MAGs and partner as a continuation to the ongoing refinement and contextualization of the approach and 2) direct rapid support to MAGs when sudden crisis emerges. If the Emergency Fund is not spent, the funds will be fully or partially re-allocated to SUDO to deliver additional grants to MAGs. ltbrgtlt/pgt
